representative_posts.author: sean-h.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: d) LLMs are a huge drain on resources (both physical and capital), they only work at all because they plagiarised *everything*, they make shit up because they can't *not* (it simply isn't how they work), their existence has made anything using RAM incredibly expensive... I could go on.

representative_posts.text: Thought, has LLMs reduced the amount of bullshit work in offices, because things can effectively be offloaded, or whether this has actually increased the amount of bullshit, as more can now be done in the same time?

representative_posts.author: jnsq.org
representative_posts.text: Machine transcription is AI. OCR document scanning is AI. Those both predate LLMs, but LLMs do them better than what came before. The important thing is preserving journalistic ethics, like "don't expose confidential sources" and "check your facts before publishing".

representative_posts.author: webofevil.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: This remains important & underpriced: LLMs cover a lot of ground very fast but only within parameters that they've been trained on & can't apply their calculations outside those parameters. representative_posts.author: slo-slo-slo.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: One of the things that LLMs and machine learning as UI do is obfuscate the nature of the tool and its relationship to the materials.
